reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is aligning surveillance imagery to a fixed bird's-eye view while handling environmental noise and minor camera shifts. This is framed as an inverse problem where the homography matrix H maps pixels from the camera frame to the reference plane. The STN learns H end-to-end, but standard MSE losses fail because they treat all pixels equally, ignoring semantic context. The topological loss addresses this by penalizing errors only within consistent semantic patches, preventing the model from being fooled by misaligned but visually similar regions. Crucially, the dictionary-based approach provides a compact prior over plausible camera poses, reducing the search space and enabling fast, robust calibration even in complex urban scenes.
